story: It is a sunny Sunday morning in Sumter Oaks, and Gary is hunched over his workbench at home, soldering the wiring for a light strip and speaker leads he plans to bolt onto his golf cart. Down on Magnolia Loop, Donna is quietly hauling extra plastic flamingos behind a hedge, leaving only three in plain view while she eyes the street with a determined look. Across the way, Hal sits at his window with binoculars, watchfully counting flamingos and sizing up whatever Gary might be cooking up for his cart. Meanwhile, Rosa is content in her kitchen, brewing a fresh pot of coffee and arranging pastries on a plate for two mugs, clearly anticipating a friendly porch visit from Hal.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Solder and wire up the light strip harness and speaker leads for the cart, bench-testing everything indoors
Donna (donna flamingo flock): Pull the extra flamingos behind the hedge, leaving just three visible from the street
Hal (hal binoculars): Scan Magnolia Loop for Donna's flamingo count and Gary's cart modifications
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Brew a fresh pot and set out two mugs and some pastries for Hal's porch visit

gary.thought_process: Morning after Halloween, I'm home with no one around, and the cart is right here. I've inspected the battery and sketched the layout twice already, so it's time to stop planning and start building. The Holiday Golf Cart Parade is the next big thing, and holiday lighting isn't allowed until Thanksgiving, so I can wire things up in the garage and test them indoors where nobody sees. Exterior mods visible from the street need Architectural Review approval (L-01), so I'll need to file that at Town Hall soon. For now, the workbench is where I can build the light strip wiring and speaker mounts out of sight. Keeping my hands busy beats rattling around this quiet house.

parameters.content: Solder and wire up the light strip harness and speaker leads for the cart, bench-testing everything indoors

donna.thought_process: Parade's over and I'm standing right next to my flamingo flock on Magnolia Loop. I promised Hal I'd thin it to three visible from the street, and L-02 caps decorative ornaments at three anyway. I already said I'd do it last tick, so now I actually do it: pull the extras behind the hedge and keep just three out front. Then I can go find Gary and talk about our next court session.

parameters.content: Pull the extra flamingos behind the hedge, leaving just three visible from the street

hal.thought_process: Halloween's over, the morning is quiet, and no one's around to talk to. Town Hall wants decorations down by November 7, which gives me a fair deadline to hold Donna's flamingos to. I've been counting her ornaments for days and I want fresh numbers before I file anything with the review committee. Best use of this hour is to pick up the binoculars and survey Magnolia Loop while the street is empty and the evidence is plain to see. Gary's cart mods and Donna's flock both belong in the notebook only if I actually see them, by the book.

parameters.content: Scan Magnolia Loop for Donna's flamingo count and Gary's cart modifications

rosa.thought_process: I've already checked my shift schedule and washed up from last night's dinner. Hal is coming for coffee on my porch later and I promised to be ready. Nobody is nearby, so there's no one to talk to. The next useful thing is to set out the coffee things properly, make the porch feel welcoming, and keep building the neighborly habit. I'll use the kitchen to get the coffee brewed and cups ready so I can enjoy the visit instead of rushing.

parameters.content: Brew a fresh pot and set out two mugs and some pastries for Hal's porch visit

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
